models.power_tree_startup / TPS72325: VENDOR - TI SLVMBZ8 unencrypted PSpice, run unmodified in ngspice PSpice mode
models.power_tree_startup / LM2664: VENDOR - TI SNVMBY1 unencrypted PSpice, run unmodified in ngspice PSpice mode
models.ldo_stability / TPS72325: behavioural HERE ONLY -- the loop-gain measurement needs a feedback terminal to break, which TI's model does not expose. power_tree_startup.py uses TI's own model for this part.
models.drl_loop / ADS1299 BIAS amp: behavioural macro; GBW swept 10 kHz..1 MHz around the datasheet 100 kHz

notes:
[power_tree_startup] LM2664 and TPS72325 use TI's own unencrypted PSpice models, run unmodified. TLV70025's TI model is encrypted and the AMS1117 has none, so those two are behavioural -- see sim/models/PROVENANCE.md. The AMS1117's load-step response is therefore optimistic and its loop stability is NOT assessed by this case.
TPS72325 ships as two silicon revisions under one part number (SLVS346E): legacy CSO DLN with 280 mV dropout, 130 uA Iq, 1 ms startup, +-3.0 %% Vout, and the newer DM6 with 140 mV, 30 uA, 8 ms, +-1.6 %%. This case runs the LEGACY parameters, which are the worse ones for dropout and accuracy.
The VCAP1..VCAP4 / VREFP capacitors (including C_VCAP1, 100 uF) hang on AVSS through ADS1299 internal nodes and are NOT in this model. Excluding them is the conservative choice for a ripple limit: more capacitance can only reduce it.
not modelled: C_VCAP1 (far side VCAP1 is not a power-tree net), C_VCAP1_H (far side VCAP1 is not a power-tree net), C_VCAP2 (far side VCAP2 is not a power-tree net), C_VCAP3 (far side VCAP3 is not a power-tree net), C_VCAP3_H (far side VCAP3 is not a power-tree net), C_VCAP4 (far side VCAP4 is not a power-tree net), C_VREFP_100n (far side VREFP is not a power-tree net), C_VREFP_10n (far side VREFP is not a power-tree net), C_VREFP_10u (far side VREFP is not a power-tree net)
[ldo_stability] Loop-gain figures come from behavioural LDO models whose internal pole is a calibration choice, so treat the phase margin as indicative and the load-step settling as the primary evidence. Both are computed on the DERATED capacitance taken from the netlist, which is the part of this result that is not model-dependent.
The DC-bias curves are Samsung's own (weblib, 25 C typical). The worst-case corner multiplies them by the tolerance low limit and by 0.85 for the X5R/X7R temperature coefficient, which is the corner a shipped board has to survive.
Capacitors reaching ADS1299 internal nodes (VCAP1..4, VREFP) are listed under *_caps_not_counted and excluded: their far side is an internal buffer whose impedance is not modelled. Including them would only add capacitance.
[drl_loop] ECO-5 check at 20 kohm skin, 100 kHz GBW: phase margin 0.7 -> 88.9 deg, DRL loop gain at 50 Hz 41.3 -> 61.0 dB, 50 Hz body common-mode suppression by the drive 6.0 -> 5.3 dB.
The BIAS amplifier is a BEHAVIOURAL two-pole macro. SBAS499 gives GBW = 100 kHz, slew rate 0.07 V/us and a 1.1 mA short-circuit limit, but not the open-loop gain or output swing, so GBW is swept a decade either side of the datasheet value and the criterion must hold across the whole sweep.
DRL EFFECTIVENESS, not a pass/fail criterion here but the more interesting number: with R_BIAS_SER at 1 Mohm the drive suppresses the 50 Hz body common mode by only about 5 dB. A right-leg drive is normally worth 20-40 dB. The loop is very stable precisely because it has so little authority, and the phase margin being flat across 5 k..100 kohm of skin is the same fact seen from another angle.
R_BIAS_SER is 1e+06 ohm. With 5..100 kohm of skin in series that is a divider of -46..-21 dB in the forward path, so the DRL's authority over the body common mode is modest by construction -- which is also why the loop is hard to destabilise.
Body model: skin = Rskin || 10 nF at every electrode, body to circuit ground = 100 pF stray, mains coupled through 5 pF. The ADS1299 internal BIAS_SENSP switch is taken as 100 ohm; the summing resistors are the board's own 10 kohm R_IN??.
[esp32_autoreset] CH340C VCC is on net USB_5V, so its DTR#/RTS# outputs swing to 5.0 V.
ABSOLUTE-MAXIMUM FINDING: with the CH340C on USB_5V its DTR#/RTS# outputs idle at 5.0 V. Both transistors are then off with a base above their 3.3 V collector, which forward-biases the base-collector junction and lifts ESP_EN and ESP_IO0 to about 4.24 V -- past the ESP32's 3.60 V maximum. The same deck with 3.3 V handshake levels peaks at 3.30 V, so this is a consequence of the CH340C's supply mode, not of the reset topology. BY INSPECTION the same concern reaches further: U_USB pin 2 TXD drives ESP_RXD (U_MCU pin 34) directly with no level shift. Confirm the CH340C's output level in 5 V supply mode against its datasheet before acting on this.
Transistors use a generic Gummel-Poon S8050 fit (BF=275, the middle of the J3Y 200..350 bin). The absolute-maximum check depends on the base-collector junction parameters, which are the least well pinned down part of that fit -- treat a marginal result as a reason to measure, not as proof.
